choices.text: Nothing: when a lamp stops, its energy has been used up and is gone for good
The energy hides inside the lamp until someone switches it on again
The energy is never used up: it changed into light and heat and moved into the room

questions.explanation: The trap is: Energy is used up, like fuel disappearing from a tank. Scene s4 shows why this is wrong: Energy is never used up: it changes form and moves somewhere else.
questions.misconception: Energy is used up, like fuel disappearing from a tank.
questions.prompt: A pupil says: when a lamp stops shining, its energy has been used up. What is wrong with this idea?

choices.text: Electrical energy, then stored energy, then sound
Electrical energy, then light and heat
Stored energy, then movement, then light only

questions.explanation: Scene s3: electrical energy travels from the battery along the wire to the bulb, where it changes into light and heat.
questions.prompt: In the torch circuit, what does the electrical energy from the battery change into at the bulb?

questions.answer: Light, heat, sound, movement and stored energy.
questions.explanation: Scene s1: light rays spread out, heat rises, sound spreads, movement slides along, and stored energy waits in its box - five forms of energy.
questions.prompt: Name the five forms of energy shown at the start of the animation.

questions.answer: It changes stored energy in its fuel into movement energy (and some heat).
questions.explanation: Scene s2: the car rolls along as the stored energy in its fuel changes into movement, with some energy leaving as heat.
questions.prompt: A car is moving along the road. What energy change is happening inside the car?

choices.text: It rises up into the air above the pot
It turns back into stored energy in the pot

questions.explanation: Scenes s1 and s2: heat rises - watch the steam puffs drift upwards as cooking heat escapes from the pot into the air.
questions.prompt: What happens to the heat energy as food cooks in a pot?
